name: Holistic SEO
seoTitle: Holistic SEO Services | Technical, On-Page & Off-Page
summary: Holistic SEO connects technical health, on-page content and relevant authority in one prioritised plan. Improve discovery and qualified enquiries.
heroTitle: Holistic SEO that connects visibility to qualified enquiries.
heroIntro: Technical fixes, useful pages and credible references work better when they support the same business goal. I bring technical, on-page and off-page SEO into one focused plan, with clear priorities, implementation ownership and measurement.
problem: A technically sound site can still answer the wrong questions. A useful page can remain undiscovered if crawling or internal links are broken. References to an unclear offer do not solve the buyer’s decision.

Holistic SEO connects these dependencies before work is prioritised. Your business goals and current evidence determine the sequence, rather than running three isolated checklists or publishing more content by default.

covers.body: Review search access, canonicals, redirects, sitemaps and internal paths to important pages.

covers.title: Rendering and page experience

covers.title: Buyer intent and page roles
covers.body: Map useful queries to service, product and resource pages with distinct jobs.

covers.title: Content, titles and headings

covers.title: Contextual internal linking

covers.title: References and relevant authority
covers.body: Assess existing links, partner opportunities and resources that real readers would want to reference.

process.title: Define the business goal
process.body: Identify priority services or products, target buyers and what a qualified action looks like. Agree the implementation scope, access and responsibilities before work starts.

process.title: Establish the baseline
process.body: Review Search Console, analytics, important templates and recent releases. Record relevant page groups, current query coverage and the contact or purchase path.

process.title: Find the connected constraints
process.body: Compare crawl and indexing evidence with page intent, useful content and relevant references. Separate confirmed defects from hypotheses and low-impact tool warnings.

process.title: Build the delivery roadmap
process.body: Choose the work that best addresses the constraint. Give tasks an owner, affected URLs, dependencies and acceptance checks so development and editorial work stay coordinated.

process.title: Implement and validate
process.body: Ship the agreed technical fixes, page improvements and reference-worthy resources. Verify the deployed HTML, links and user journey before treating a task as complete.

process.title: Measure and refine
process.body: Review the changed page groups and qualified actions against the baseline. Account for seasonality, tracking and other releases, then use the evidence to choose the next priorities.

faqs.q: What is holistic SEO?
faqs.a: Holistic SEO treats technical access, useful page content, relevant references and the user’s next step as one connected system. The work is prioritised around business goals and evidence instead of treating each discipline as an isolated checklist.

faqs.q: Does this include technical, on-page and off-page SEO?
faqs.a: Yes. These three disciplines are brought into one plan. The proposal defines the pages, templates, deliverables and implementation responsibilities included, so the scope fits the constraint rather than assuming every possible SEO task is needed.

faqs.q: Where do we start if our website has several problems?
faqs.a: Start with the issues affecting important buying pages and qualified actions. Crawl or indexing barriers may need attention before a content release; unclear intent or a broken enquiry path may matter more than acquiring additional references. The baseline guides the order.

faqs.q: Do you implement changes or work with our team?
faqs.a: Both arrangements can be discussed. I can provide writer-ready briefs and developer tickets, collaborate with your existing team or implement within an agreed platform scope. Ownership, approval and post-release checks are defined before the work begins.

faqs.q: How is holistic SEO different from a one-off audit?
faqs.a: An audit diagnoses the current situation and recommends priorities. A holistic engagement can also coordinate implementation, validate releases and review outcomes over time. The proposal makes clear whether you are buying analysis, implementation support or ongoing review.

faqs.q: How long does it take to see SEO results?
faqs.a: There is no fixed ranking or lead timeline. Scope, competition, site history and implementation speed matter. First confirm that the work is shipped and accessible, then review meaningful periods of relevant queries and qualified actions with seasonality and other changes in view.

faqs.q: What affects the cost of holistic SEO?
faqs.a: The number of pages and templates, research depth, editorial needs, development requirements and reporting scope affect cost. Share your URL, priorities and available team for a scoped proposal. Extra production, third-party fees and specialist review are not assumed to be included.

faqs.q: Do you buy backlinks or guarantee rankings?
faqs.a: No ranking position or lead volume is guaranteed. Off-page work focuses on relevant editorial references, useful resources and genuine partner opportunities. Paid ranking schemes and fabricated proof are not part of the plan.

faqs.q: How do you measure whether the work is helping?
faqs.a: Track the agreed landing-page groups, relevant query visibility, qualified enquiries or sales and the specific defects addressed. Keep a release log and reporting baseline. Explain attribution limits instead of claiming every business change was caused by SEO.

faqs.q: What do you need before we discuss a plan?
faqs.a: Your website URL, priority products or services, target market and main growth constraint are enough for an initial discussion. Search Console, analytics, CMS access and a developer or editorial contact help once the project scope is agreed.

ctaLine: Give your SEO work one direction and a clear next step.

engagement.title: How connected SEO work looks in practice
engagement.intro: The first priority is the constraint holding back your important pages. The next priority is the dependency that makes the improvement useful for a buyer.

priorities.title: Make the page accessible
priorities.body: Confirm the preferred URL, crawl access, rendered information and internal path. Fix the technical blocker before asking the content or outreach team to build on it.

priorities.title: Make the answer useful
priorities.body: Improve the page around its audience and task, with approved evidence, clear scope and an appropriate next action. Useful detail matters more than a target word count.

priorities.title: Make the destination worth referencing
priorities.body: Connect relevant resources and genuine partner opportunities to pages that serve readers. Editorial coverage is another organisation’s decision, not a deliverable that can be guaranteed.

example.title: Example: a service page gets impressions but few useful enquiries
example.body: An illustrative workflow starts by checking the page’s status, canonical and rendered content. Next, review whether the queries match the offer and whether scope, trust information and contact details answer the buying decision. Improve the relevant internal paths and reference-worthy supporting resources, then compare qualified actions after release.

engagement.measurement: Review technical completion, relevant page-group visibility and qualified actions together. Search Console provides query and landing-page context; analytics and sales feedback help assess enquiry relevance. Keep releases, campaigns and seasonal demand beside the reporting baseline, and distinguish observed change from a claim of direct causation.
preparation: Website URL, priority offers and target audiences
Search Console and analytics access when scope is agreed
CMS or developer contact, editorial capacity and approved evidence

name: Content SEO
summary: Content SEO strategy, topic maps, writer-ready briefs and targeted refreshes. Build useful pages around buyer questions and commercial priorities.
heroTitle: Content SEO planned around buyer questions and search demand.
heroIntro: Publishing more doesn't build authority. Publishing the right topics, in the right order, connected in the right way, does. I build content strategies your team can execute and briefs your writers can actually use.
problem: A lot of company blogs are a list of unrelated posts. Each one gets a burst of social traffic and then nothing, because none of them build towards a topic Google trusts the site on.
Content SEO means mapping the questions your buyers ask across the whole journey, then covering those topics more usefully than anyone else ranking today.

covers.title: Topical maps
covers.body: The full set of subjects you need to cover to be seen as an authority, grouped into clusters.

covers.title: SERP analysis
covers.body: What ranks, why it ranks, and what gap a new page can fill.

covers.title: Content briefs
covers.body: Intent, angle, outline, questions to answer, internal links and examples — everything a writer needs.

covers.title: Information architecture
covers.body: Hub pages, categories and URL structure that make clusters obvious to users and crawlers.

covers.title: Content refreshes
covers.body: Updating decaying articles before they lose their positions.

covers.title: Content pruning
covers.body: Merging, redirecting or removing pages that dilute quality.

process.title: Inventory content and buyer questions
process.body: Review existing pages, sales questions and search data. Classify useful material, coverage gaps and pages that overlap or need a factual update.

process.title: Plan topic and page roles
process.body: Choose which topics belong in guides, use-case pages or comparisons. Set priorities around the product and the team’s capacity to deliver useful content.

process.title: Brief, review and publish
process.body: Prepare outlines, evidence requirements, internal links and review responsibilities. Check accuracy and the reader’s next step before publication.

process.title: Maintain and measure the library
process.body: Track new and refreshed pages separately. Update information when the offer or evidence changes and review the qualified actions the content supports.

useCases.title: Building a topic cluster
useCases.body: A useful hub supported by focused articles with clear page roles and relevant links. Each page still needs to answer a distinct question; linking a cluster does not guarantee rankings.

useCases.title: Decay recovery
useCases.body: Finding articles that have lost clicks year on year and refreshing them with current information and better structure.

faqs.q: How much content do we need to publish?
faqs.a: Less than most people think. A consistent cadence of genuinely useful pages beats high volume. The topical map tells us how much ground there is to cover.

faqs.q: Do you write the content?
faqs.a: My focus is strategy, briefs and optimisation. I work alongside your writers or recommended writers, and review drafts for search alignment.

faqs.q: Can AI-written content rank?
faqs.a: Content ranks when it's useful, accurate and original enough to add something. How it's produced matters less than whether it has real expertise and a reason to exist.

ctaLine: Publishing content that isn't moving the numbers?

engagement.title: From content inventory to a publishable editorial plan
engagement.intro: The first decision is often whether to improve an existing page, combine overlapping material or create something that is genuinely missing.

priorities.title: Give every topic a job
priorities.body: Separate educational guidance from comparison, use-case and service content. A brief records the intended audience, question, page format and relevant commercial next step.

priorities.title: Build in original evidence
priorities.body: Identify the product screenshots, interviews, practical examples or first-hand observations that make a page useful. Sensitive topics need an appropriate subject reviewer before publication.

priorities.title: Plan maintenance as well as publishing
priorities.body: Record who owns each topic and what would trigger an update. Preserve useful URLs and check links before merging or removing pages with traffic or backlinks.

example.title: Example: a SaaS blog attracts readers outside its market
example.body: Instead of adding another broad article, I map customer questions to existing guides and product use cases. A refreshed guide can explain a real workflow and link to the product feature that supports it, while a separate comparison page answers the purchase decision.

engagement.measurement: Review relevant query coverage, organic landing-page visits and the actions those pages assist. Keep new pages and refreshed pages separate in reporting. Editorial output is a delivery measure; qualified product or service interest is the business measure.

Access to writers and subject-matter reviewers

name: Local SEO
summary: Local SEO for eligible Business Profiles, service pages and real coverage areas. Improve local discovery and measure qualified calls and enquiries.
heroTitle: Local SEO for businesses that win customers nearby.
heroIntro: Local customers discover businesses through Maps and organic search. I improve eligible Business Profiles, useful service and area pages, business information and the mobile contact path, with reporting focused on qualified enquiries.
problem: Local rankings depend on proximity, relevance and prominence. You can't move your address, but you can control how relevant and prominent your business looks to Google.
Many businesses have an incomplete Business Profile, inconsistent contact details across the web, and one generic service page trying to rank in every area they serve.

covers.title: Google Business Profile
covers.body: Eligible profile setup, accurate categories, services, attributes, hours and imagery. Available profile features are reviewed for your business and market.

covers.title: Local landing pages

covers.title: Citations & NAP consistency

covers.title: Review strategy

covers.title: Local keyword research

covers.title: Local links

process.title: Confirm eligibility and coverage
process.body: Review the real operating model, customer contact details, hours and served areas before changing Business Profile or website information.

process.title: Audit the local discovery path
process.body: Compare profile details, service and area pages, customer-location results and the mobile enquiry experience. Identify inconsistent or missing information.

process.title: Improve profiles and priority pages
process.body: Apply agreed profile changes, strengthen useful service pages and establish an honest review request process. Keep website and business details aligned.

process.title: Measure qualified local actions

faqs.q: Do I need a physical address for local SEO?
faqs.a: Eligible service-area businesses that travel to customers can hide their address. They still need a genuine operating base and must meet Google’s in-person service rules. Online-only businesses and virtual-office setups do not qualify simply because they target a city.

faqs.q: How important are reviews?
faqs.a: Google says review count and positive ratings can help local ranking. Helpful replies support customer trust; reply quality is not presented as a guaranteed ranking factor. Ask genuine customers for honest feedback without incentives or review gating.

faqs.q: Should I create a page for every city I serve?
faqs.a: Only where you have something specific to say. Thin city pages can hurt more than help. Fewer, better location pages usually win.

ctaLine: Missing from the map pack in your area?

engagement.title: A local SEO plan that reflects how the business operates
engagement.intro: The website and Business Profile should tell the same accurate story about services, contact details and where customers can actually receive them.

priorities.title: Confirm profile eligibility and details
priorities.body: Check the actual business model, categories and customer-facing information. Storefronts and service-area businesses have different setups; a fabricated office is not a shortcut to local visibility.

priorities.title: Improve useful service and area pages
priorities.body: Explain coverage, availability and the booking process. Add local experience only where it is real, and connect area pages to the relevant services instead of duplicating the same text.

priorities.title: Make contact easy to complete
priorities.body: Test mobile call links, quote forms, opening hours and directions where relevant. Request honest reviews after genuine experiences without incentives or filtering for positive feedback.

example.title: Example: a contractor appears near its base but needs better website enquiries
example.body: I separate map visibility from organic service-page discovery. The plan may improve the main profile, clarify coverage and strengthen a service page for a town already served. Changing the service-area setting does not remove Google’s distance factor.

engagement.measurement: Track Business Profile interactions, organic visits to local pages, qualified calls and completed forms where measurement is available. Review visibility from relevant customer locations rather than relying on one ranking at the business address.

problem: A good reputation offline does not always translate into visibility online. If competitors appear for your core services while your website relies on one generic page, homeowners may never discover your business.

More traffic is only useful when it brings the right jobs. I build an SEO plan around your service area, profitable services and capacity, then connect search visibility to qualified calls and quote requests so you can see what is working.

faqs.q: Which home service businesses do you work with?
faqs.a: This service is designed for plumbers, HVAC companies, electricians, roofers, septic providers, cleaners, landscapers, pest control businesses and other contractors. The strategy is tailored to the services and areas your team actually covers.

faqs.q: How is this different from general local SEO?
faqs.a: Local SEO is part of the work. Home service SEO also considers individual job types, emergency versus planned demand, seasonal services, coverage limits and the website experience that turns a homeowner search into a useful enquiry.

faqs.q: Can you help with Google Business Profile and my website?
faqs.a: Yes. I review how your profile and website support each other, then prioritise profile improvements, service pages, area pages and technical fixes. The implementation scope is agreed before the work begins.

faqs.q: Do I need a page for every town I serve?
faqs.a: No. Start with the areas that matter to your business and where you can provide useful, distinct information. Pages should reflect real service availability and local experience rather than repeating the same content with a different town name.

faqs.q: How long does home service SEO take to show results?
faqs.a: Timing depends on your starting point, local competition and how quickly changes are implemented. We establish a baseline and review progress over the following months. I do not guarantee a ranking position or a fixed number of leads.

faqs.q: How will we measure whether the SEO is working?
faqs.a: We agree on useful business measures such as qualified calls, quote requests and booked-job data where available. Organic traffic, page performance and local visibility provide context; lead quality helps decide the next priorities.

faqs.q: Can SEO work alongside paid ads?
faqs.a: Yes. SEO can build discovery through service pages and local search while ads address immediate demand. We can use enquiry data from both channels to understand which services and locations deserve more attention.

faqs.q: What do you need to get started?
faqs.a: Your website URL, core services, coverage areas and growth priorities are enough for an initial discussion. For the audit, access to Search Console, analytics and Google Business Profile helps identify the most useful next steps.

ctaLine: Ready to turn local searches into your next booked job?

priorities.title: Separate urgent and planned work
priorities.body: Emergency repair pages need truthful availability and a direct mobile call path. Installation and replacement pages need assessment details, decision guidance and a clear quote process.

priorities.title: Show the work behind the offer
priorities.body: Use authorised job photos, accurate service scope and genuine customer feedback. Explain what an assessment covers and which details are needed before an estimate can be given.

priorities.title: Match coverage to operations
priorities.body: Prioritise towns and neighbourhoods the team reliably serves. Use dispatch boundaries and job records to guide area pages, rather than creating pages for every nearby place.

example.title: Example: a septic provider wants more replacement requests
example.body: A replacement page can explain assessment, access requirements and how a homeowner requests a quote. It should distinguish replacement from routine pumping and repair, then connect those related services. Photos and project details must come from real authorised work.

engagement.measurement: Review qualified enquiries by service and area, with booked jobs or job value where available. Exclude spam and requests outside coverage. Annotate busy seasons and staffing constraints so more search traffic is not mistaken for greater booking capacity.

name: E-commerce SEO
summary: E-commerce SEO for categories, products and catalogue indexing. Improve shopping pages, filter handling and markup with organic sales reporting.
heroTitle: E-commerce SEO built around how shoppers search.
heroIntro: E-commerce SEO connects category and product pages to shopping intent. I improve catalogue structure, useful product information, filter handling and internal links, then review organic orders and revenue alongside indexing.
problem: Filters and sorting options can turn a 500-product store into 500,000 URLs. Google spends its time crawling duplicates while new products wait to be indexed.
Meanwhile the category pages that should rank for high-intent searches often have no copy, weak internal links and titles generated by the platform.

covers.title: Category optimisation
covers.body: Category structure and copy built around the way shoppers search, including sub-categories for high-demand attributes.

covers.title: Product pages
covers.body: Unique descriptions, useful specs, reviews and handling of variants and out-of-stock items.

covers.title: Faceted navigation
covers.body: Selecting useful filter landing pages and aligning crawl, canonical and indexing rules for the rest. Blocking crawling and excluding a page from indexing are different decisions.

covers.title: Product schema
covers.body: Product, Offer, Review and Breadcrumb markup for rich results and Merchant listings.

covers.title: Internal linking
covers.body: Related categories, breadcrumbs and collections that spread authority across the catalogue.

covers.title: Platform SEO
covers.body: Shopify, WooCommerce and headless commerce limitations and workarounds.

process.title: Review shopping paths and stock
process.body: Start with priority categories, product demand, inventory and sales data. Identify where catalogue structure fails to match how customers shop.

process.title: Map category and filter decisions
process.body: Select useful category opportunities and define handling for filters, variants and pagination. Test crawl and indexing rules before a wider rollout.

process.title: Improve templates and product facts
process.body: Update category context, unique product information and relevant markup. Check that price, availability and offer details match the live catalogue.

process.title: Validate and review organic sales
process.body: Retest indexable paths and structured data, then review category and product landing-page orders and revenue with stock and promotion context.

deliverables: Category keyword map and structure recommendations
Faceted navigation indexing rules
Product page templates and copy guidelines
Schema implementation
Platform-specific technical fixes
commonProblems: Thousands of filter URLs indexed
New products slow to appear in search
Category pages outranked by marketplaces
Duplicate manufacturer descriptions
Lost rankings after a platform migration
whoFor: Brands competing with marketplaces for category terms

useCases.title: Attribute landing pages
useCases.body: Creating indexable pages for high-demand filter combinations — like material or size — while keeping the rest out of the index.

useCases.title: Seasonal categories
useCases.body: Keeping seasonal URLs live year-round so they keep their authority for next season.

faqs.q: Should product descriptions be unique?
faqs.a: For products you want to rank, yes. Manufacturer copy appears on every retailer's site. Even a short, original section about use cases or fit helps.

faqs.q: What should happen to discontinued products?
faqs.a: It depends on whether the page has links or traffic and whether a close replacement exists. Options include keeping it with alternatives, redirecting, or returning a 410.

faqs.q: Is Shopify good for SEO?
faqs.a: It's a solid foundation with some fixed URL patterns and duplicate-path quirks. Most issues can be managed with templates, apps used carefully and good internal linking.

ctaLine: Catalogue growing faster than your organic traffic?

engagement.title: Catalogue SEO that keeps shopping and indexing aligned
engagement.intro: Category, product and filter pages have different jobs. The right plan makes high-demand shopping paths discoverable without filling search with duplicates.

priorities.title: Prioritise categories with a clear shopping need
priorities.body: Review demand, available stock and existing sales before adding categories. Keep helpful copy close to the product grid without obstructing browsing or replacing product information.

priorities.title: Define filter and variant rules
priorities.body: Decide which combinations deserve stable landing pages. Align canonical, crawl and indexing rules; a crawler cannot read a noindex instruction on a URL blocked by robots.txt.

priorities.title: Keep product facts consistent
priorities.body: Check specifications, availability and price against the live catalogue. Product and offer markup should describe the visible product, while reviews must reflect genuine review content.

example.title: Example: material filters create duplicate category URLs
example.body: A store might have useful demand for linen shirts but dozens of low-value sort and filter combinations. I map the genuine shopping intent to a stable category, link it from relevant navigation and test how the remaining combinations are handled before wider rollout.

engagement.measurement: Measure category and product landing-page revenue, orders and relevant organic visits. Check priority product indexing and structured-data errors. Stock changes, discounts and checkout changes belong in the report because they can affect conversion independently of SEO.
preparation: Search Console and ecommerce analytics access
Top categories, margin priorities and planned promotions
